blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang finds no need to declare a state of calamity yet in areas affected by El Niño, as government agencies concerned are already working to mitigate its impact. This comes after 20 senators introduced Senate Resolution No. 765. The resolution was passed to “urge the President of the Philippines, upon the recommendation of the National Disaster and Risk Reduction Management Council and in accordance with applicable laws, to declare a state of calamity… in areas experiencing drought-related disaster impacts.” READ: Senators to Marcos: Declare state of calamity in El Niño affected areas At a briefing on Tuesday, Castro said […]...
